title: Deploy qualifier: quota, IAM, DNS, and GPU SKU prober for Private installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a cross-cloud 'deploy-qualifier' utility and integration hooks that run a bounded set of sanity checks prior to Private (VPC) installs. The tool must verify: (1) account and regional quotas (vCPUs, GPUs, network IPs, load balancers), (2) required IAM roles/policies and STS assume-role paths for the installer and runtime agents, (3) DNS zone delegation, resolvability and reverse lookup for control plane endpoints, and (4) GPU SKU availability and basic VM provisioning smoke (spot/ondemand). The output should be both human-readable and machine-parsable JSON with clear remediation advice and a non-zero exit code for blocking failures. Support AWS and GCP for initial rollout; design extension points for Azure. Integrate as a step in the Terraform-based installer pipeline and provide a lightweight GitHub Actions runner and a one-shot CLI for SEs onboarding customers.
acceptance_criteria: A CLI binary (or Python entrypoint) 'redwood-deploy-qualifier' that runs checks for AWS and GCP and returns structured JSON summary
Checks for account-level quotas and per-region limits with examples and link to console where quota can be increased
IAM validation: verifies existence of required roles/policies and that the installer can assume them (STS dry-run) without exposing secrets
DNS validation: confirms that control plane domain is delegated, A/AAAA records resolve from multiple public resolvers, and reverse PTR exists for the control endpoint IP where applicable
GPU probe: queries region SKU availability and performs a non-destructive VM create-and-delete smoke on a configurable instance type to confirm provisioning path
Integration: automatically runnable from the Terraform plan/apply CI step and as a pre-deploy gate in the installer workflow
Machine-readable report stored in S3/GCS for triage dashboards and included in installer logs
Documentation: step-by-step remediation guide and examples for common failures in Confluence
steps: Design API and output schema (JSON + exit codes) - link to design doc
Implement modular checks: quotas, iam, dns, gpu. Keep cloud provider adapters small and testable
Add GitHub Action + TF hook that calls CLI and uploads report to artifacts
Add unit and integration tests (mock cloud APIs + one live smoke region)
Run canary on two existing customer VPCs and iterate on error messages
Ship initial release behind feature-flag and monitor false-positive rate for 2 weeks
notes: Trade-offs: deep quota reconciliation (enumerating every AWS service) is out-of-scope for v1 — focus on resources we know the installer consumes: EC2 vCPUs/GPU SKUs, ENIs/EIPs, ALBs, IAM roles, and route53/GCP DNS.

Permissions: the qualifier should run with minimal read-only permissions where possible. GPU smoke requires ephemeral create/delete privileges; provide an opt-out flag for customers who can't grant it.
Performance: CLI should complete within 90s for common cases. GPU smoke increases runtime — make it optional with a fast SKU-check path that only queries SKU availability.
Extensibility: design provider adapter interface for Azure/OCI later. Output schema must include 'provider' and 'check_version' fields for forward compatibility.
